title: Container ABI Protector & SBOM Drift Detector for LTS Channels
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we maintain multiple LTS channels and CI-built container images, we see frequent subtle mismatches between the SBOM/manifest and the runtime kernel/CUDA ABI used by the image. These mismatches cause a small but recurrent class of failures in Dedicated/private deploys (driver incompatibility, missing transitive libraries, and silent perf regressions) that are hard to triage during rollouts.

Goal: Build an automated "Container ABI Protector" that continuously compares image SBOMs and signed provenance metadata against a canonical ABI compatibility matrix and flags (or auto-blocks) images whose declared/observed runtime kernel, libc, or CUDA runtime are outside the allowed pinset for a target LTS channel. Provide observability (drift dashboard) and an actionable remediation workflow (pin suggestions, automated rollback, or staging-only tagging).

Scope:
- Ingest SBOMs and image manifests from the artifact registry and map declared runtime deps (glibc, kernel headers, CUDA runtime, libcuda) to our ABI catalog.
- Run a lightweight runtime probe during CI image promotion that validates kernel symbols, CUDA driver/runtime compatibility, and a small runtime smoke test to detect missing transitive libs.
- Surface SBOM drift (attested vs observed divergence) in a new Drift Dashboard and emit rollout-gate signals that can block promotion to LTS channels.
- Provide an API to propose pinset fixes (e.g., suggest concrete driver package versions or a compatible base image) and a "soft-fail" staging mode to collect telemetry before stricter enforcement.

Out of scope for this ticket: auto-rebuilding images with fixed pins (will be next-phase), full attestation of vendor driver binaries, and cross-region image replication concerns.
acceptance_criteria: A CI hook exists that fetches the SBOM and runs an image probe verifying declared vs observed runtime libs for new image promotions.
Images with mismatches are flagged in the artifact registry and included in the Drift Dashboard with root-cause hints (missing symbol, mismatched CUDA ABI, transitive library absent).
Rollout-gate integration configured: LTS promotion pipelines can opt-in to block images with high-severity drift; gates expose clear remediation suggestions.
A minimal remediation workflow in Console: link to proposed pinset changes and a GitHub issue template created automatically for the image owner.
Smoke tests for a sample of Dedicated/private clusters show reduced driver/ABI failures in canary promotions after opt-in enforcement (compare baseline to post-enforcement metrics).
notes: Initial ABI catalog maintained in repo: github.com/redwood/abi-catalog (read-only for this ticket).
We will reuse parts of the existing SBOM ingestion pipeline but must extend it to include runtime probe hooks.
Security: we will not pause image promotion on unsigned SBOMs in phase 1; that will be handled in a follow-up security hardening sprint.

2026-02-18 - Tomás Ruiz: Spike completed. Implemented a prototype probe that checks /usr/lib for expected SONAMEs and validates CUDA runtime version via nvml. Prototype found 8 mismatches in last 30 images (mostly base-image drift).
2026-02-25 - Mei Chen (SRE): Recommended we classify mismatches by severity (missing symbol -> P0, minor version skew -> P2). Will provide mapping table.
2026-03-03 - Tomás Ruiz: Draft PR for CI hook submitted: github.com/redwood/runtime-ci/pull/314. The hook runs SBOM parse -> probe -> drift-report JSON artifact.
2026-03-09 - Jordan Brooks (Release): Requested gating control to be opt-in per LTS channel and ability to set enforcement level (soft, warn, block).
2026-03-12 - Tomás Ruiz: Dashboard skeleton deployed to staging Grafana. Added panels for "images flagged", "mismatch types", and "top offending base images". Next: wire alerts and the gating API.
